skill.name: git-workspace-init
skill.description: Guides an AI assistant through creating a Git worktree, conventional branch name, and remote tracking branch for isolated development work.
skill.summary: Create an isolated Git worktree with a conventional branch name and optional remote tracking setup.
skill.author: BillChirico

security_audit.summary: AI review found the high static score was caused by Markdown examples and intended Git workflow commands. The subprocess and shell examples use fixed Git commands or argument-list subprocess calls, with no prompt injection, stealth exfiltration, or arbitrary command execution evidence. The remaining risk is operational because the workflow can create worktrees, fetch from origin, and push branches when executed.

remediation.issue: Remote branch creation is included in the default workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for explicit user confirmation before running git push -u origin and show the target remote first.

remediation.issue: Helper examples accept branch and base branch strings before Git commands.
remediation.suggestion: Validate branch and base names before execution, and reject values that start with dashes or contain control characters.

remediation.issue: The examples can change local filesystem state by creating .worktrees directories.
remediation.suggestion: Present a dry-run summary of the worktree path and base branch before creating directories or branches.

content.value_statement: Starting parallel Git work can require branch naming, worktree setup, and remote tracking steps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a repeatable workspace initialization workflow.
actual_capabilities: Prompts for a task type and short task description before branch creation.
Formats branch names with conventional prefixes such as feat, fix, docs, and chore.
Places new worktrees under a .worktrees directory at the repository root.
Shows Git commands for creating a branch from a chosen base branch.
Includes optional remote tracking setup with git push -u origin.
Documents cleanup commands for removing worktrees and stale branch references.
limitations: Requires an existing Git repository with a configured remote.
Assumes origin/main unless the user supplies another base branch.
Does not inspect repository branch protection or team naming policies.
Git commands can change local and remote repository state when executed.

use_cases.title: Start Feature Work
use_cases.description: Create a feature branch and isolated worktree before implementing new application behavior.

use_cases.title: Prepare Bug Fixes
use_cases.description: Open a focused worktree for a fix while keeping the main checkout untouched.

use_cases.title: Run Parallel AI Tasks
use_cases.description: Give an AI coding assistant separate workspaces for independent tasks in one repository.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Feature Workspace
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup with default base branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use git-workspace-init for a feat branch named user authentication. Use main as the base branch.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Bug Fix Workspace
prompt_templates.scenario: Confirm the planned branch and location first.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an isolated worktree for a fix called login validation error. Show the branch name and path before running commands.

prompt_templates.title: Use a Release Base
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate setup with a non-default base branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Initialize a docs worktree for API reference update from release/2.0. Confirm the Git commands before pushing the branch.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Parallel Worktrees
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for multiple independent tasks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan two separate worktrees for a refactor and a test update. Use concise branch names and explain cleanup steps.

output_examples.input: Start a feature workspace for dark mode.
output_examples.output: The assistant proposes feat/dark-mode, creates a .worktrees/feat-dark-mode workspace, and reports the next terminal location.

output_examples.input: Create a bug fix worktree for login validation error.
output_examples.output: The assistant proposes fix/login-validation-error, checks the repository root, and prepares a tracked branch on origin.

output_examples.input: Clean up the worktree after merge.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains how to remove the worktree, delete the merged local branch, and prune stale remote references.

best_practices: Review the proposed branch name before any Git command runs.
Confirm the base branch matches the repository workflow.
Remove worktrees after merge to keep the repository clean.
anti_patterns: Do not run the workflow outside a Git repository.
Do not push a branch before confirming the target remote.
Do not reuse an existing branch name for unrelated work.

faq.question: Does this skill create a new repository?
faq.answer: No. It works inside an existing Git repository and creates an additional worktree.

faq.question: Can I choose a base branch other than main?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples allow a base branch value such as release/2.0 or develop.

faq.question: Does it push code automatically?
faq.answer: The workflow includes a remote tracking push. Users should confirm the command before execution.

faq.question: What branch naming style does it use?
faq.answer: It uses conventional prefixes such as feat, fix, hotfix, docs, refactor, test, chore, perf, ci, and style.

faq.question: Can it manage several tasks at once?
faq.answer: Yes. Git worktrees let separate branches exist in separate directories for parallel work.

faq.question: Does it remove worktrees after a pull request merges?
faq.answer: It documents cleanup commands, but the user must decide when to remove each worktree.
